A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey, with matching task taxonomies and original diagnostic experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and references support comparison. All 37 pages of v1 and 66 pages of v2 are accessible; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original AdAM experiments: 10-shot FFHQ-to-Flowers adaptation yields FID 124.46, and three randomly selected AFHQ-Cat training sets yield FIDs 90.0, 71.6, and 49.9 (Section 3.2, Figures 6–7).

after.justification: v2 retains those original AdAM experiments and outcomes in Section 4.2 and Figures 6–7. Section 6.2 additionally reports quantitative and qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: The work remains a survey with the same eight-task and seven-approach taxonomies. Expanded descriptions and comparisons of published methods do not introduce a proposed algorithm or establish changes to the methods used in the retained diagnostic experiments.

E1.justification: Section 6.2 substantially expands reported evaluation coverage within the retained taxonomy. New comparisons include Food101, C101 and DTD, explicit Human-to-Werewolf and Photo-to-Sketch scenarios, and SinDDM and DreamBooth benchmarks (Tables 7–12), beyond v1's diagnostic evaluations.

E2.justification: v2 introduces extensive evaluated comparison sets absent from v1's corresponding reporting. Table 6 compares TGAN, FreezeD, EWC, CDC, DCL, AdAM, and RICK; Table 7 compares NADA, IPL, SVL, and AIR. Other new tables add comparisons for conditional, internal-patch, and subject-driven generation.

E3.justification: The added comparisons introduce task-specific evaluation designs: 100-shot training in Table 5, FFHQ-pretrained StyleGAN2 comparisons in Tables 6–7, settings following CbC and VPT, and measurements including DINO, CLIP-I, CLIP-T, LPIPS, and SIFID. The original AdAM protocols remain unchanged. These additions do not establish that every quantitative result was newly rerun.

E4.justification: Figures 8–10 add illustrative comparisons of source-content retention, zero-shot semantic adaptation, and subject fidelity across methods. Section 7.2 also adds temporal breakdowns of research approaches. The original domain-proximity, remote-transfer, and sample-selection analyses in Figures 5–7 are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three randomly selected 10-shot AFHQ-Cat training sets. The new benchmark tables provide point estimates without introducing repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 5–12 add substantial numerical and qualitative results; for example, Table 6 reports RICK FIDs of 39.39 on FFHQ-Baby and 53.27 on AFHQ-Cat. Figure 3 updates literature statistics, including diffusion-model coverage from 12% to 30%. The original Flowers FID and three sample-selection results remain unchanged; the added scores are not paired performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: v1's explicit IPL prompt-mapper definition in Equation 8 and accompanying prompt/domain-embedding construction are omitted from v2's shorter account. The task definitions, background equations, and augmentation-invariance relation remain. NADA's directional loss is retained inline rather than removed.

C1.justification: The principal contribution claims—comprehensive GM-DC coverage, two novel taxonomies, and task–approach–method interactions—remain. v2 adds critical analysis and empirical comparison to the contribution statement and increases claimed survey coverage from 113 to 233 papers, without redefining the central research objective.

C2.justification: New Section 6.1 develops extensive success conditions, failure mechanisms, limitations, and design recommendations for individual approach categories. Section 5.1.5 also qualifies CLIP offset alignment through the added AIR discussion. Some new interpretations are inconsistent: Section 6.2 attributes CbC's results to contrastive strategies, whereas Section 5.3.3 describes progressive conditioning.

D1.justification: v2 documents search keywords, repositories, inclusion criteria, and a second search round in Section 1.1. It adds implementation-provenance information for visual comparisons and updates the project-site address. Some earlier technical detail is condensed, including IPL's mapper construction and HyperDomainNet's 6K trainable-parameter count.

R1.justification: The surveyed literature expands from 113 to 233 works, including substantial recent coverage of methods such as DANI, AIR, and MoMA. A new Related Work section distinguishes the survey from discriminative few-shot learning surveys, general generative-model surveys, and the earlier limited-data GAN survey.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, adds search-strategy and Related Work sections, inserts a substantial critical-analysis section, and reorganizes existing transfer-learning and language-guided reviews into thematic subsections. Author information and citation style also change. This is extensive restructuring beyond simple renumbering.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the expanded Sankey diagram and publication charts, adds Tables 5–12 and Figures 8–12, and transposes the metric overview in Table 4. The document uses a different layout, with retained figures and tables resized and redistributed across pages.

improvement.justification: Relative to v1, v2 offers clearer literature-selection documentation, broader coverage, and useful cross-task comparisons. However, its new synthesis introduces reliability problems: it claims RICK leads diversity on both domains although Table 6 gives AFHQ-Cat CDC 0.629 versus RICK 0.569, and mischaracterizes CbC as contrastive despite its own progressive-conditioning description. These errors affect the added practical guidance, making the net balance between greater comprehensiveness and interpretive reliability uncertain.
